newsitem.title: USA: Firms gave Dems millions, reaped billions - report.
newsitem.headline: Firms gave Dems millions, reaped billions - report.

text.p: U.S. businesses that gave Democratic Party committees more than $2.3 million in donations won coveted seats on U.S. trade missions and eventually got nearly $5.5 billion in federal aid to support foreign operations, The Boston Globe reported on Sunday.

Some 27 corporations that sent executives on trade trips with the late Commerce Secretary Ron Brown during President Clinton's first term obtained part of a multibillion-dollar commitment in federally guaranteed assistance from the Overseas Private Investment Corp (OPIC), the Globe reported.
OPIC provides insurance and loan guarantees generally not available on the commercial market because of risk.

Citing a review of federal records, the Globe said all but three of 27 recipients donated to Democratic Party committees, with the donations ranging from $50,000 to $358,000. The average contribution to the Democrats from OPIC recipients on Brown's trips was nearly $95,000 and the average support the agency gave the 27 was about $200 million, the newspaper said.

Brown died with 34 others on a trade mission to Bosnia when their Air Force plane crashed in April 1996. Four of the crash victims were executives with AT&T Bechtel Corp, Foster Wheeler Corp and Harza Engineering.
